question: Strimzi 1.3.1, Kafka 4.3, 6 brokers, JBOD with one 2 TB volume each. Last month we switched the Kafka resource to quotas of type strimzi with generous producer and consumer byte rates, plus our usual settings. Since about 07:00 every producer of every team is slow: send latency p99 went from 20 ms to 4 s and a few services log TimeoutException after max.block.ms on buffer allocation. Consumers look normal. No deploys today. Per-user quotas on our KafkaUsers are far above the actual traffic. Grafana shows broker 3's data volume at 91% used, the others at 60-70%. We upgraded Argo CD from 2.13 to 3.6.1 last month; our Helm values for argocd-cm were carried over unchanged, including the resource tracking setting we had back then. Yesterday we renamed the Argo CD Application that deploys our Strimzi 1.3.1 Kafka resource from kafka-prod-app to prod, so that it matches the Kafka resource name prod. Since then the Application lists about 60 extra resources created by the Strimzi operator (Services including prod-kafka-bootstrap, Secrets, ConfigMaps, PVCs, pods), all marked as requiring pruning. Auto-sync has prune turned off. A colleague wants to run a sync with prune to clean up the view. What is going on and what should we do?

During the nightly model reload they have stop-the-world GC pauses of up to 70 s. On the old protocol this was fine because we ran with session.timeout.ms=120000, and we kept that setting. Now, every night, members are fenced and their partitions move around for half an hour. Why, and how do we fix it?

Legal requires that after an erasure request the user's data is gone from the topic within 30 days. Local broker disks are our biggest cost, so we want older data in object storage. We also have a compacted topic, audit-index, that we would like to move the same way.
